result.rationale: The diff replaces the axios call for Zoho CRM with `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`, which (per its implementation in the new refreshOAuthTokens.ts) returns a raw fetch `Response` when credential sharing is enabled. The unchanged line `if (!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error)` assumes an axios response with `.data`; a fetch Response has no `.data`, so accessing `.error` throws a TypeError on sharing-enabled deployments. Same mechanism applies to the other refresh callers (e.g. hubspot, zoho-bigin) whose downstream code assumes axios shapes, confirming the pattern is real.

judged_text: With sharing enabled `zohoCrmTokenInfo` is a fetch Response, which has no `.data` property, so the unchanged `if (!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error)` throws a TypeError (reading 'error' of undefined). Zoho CRM token refresh always throws on sharing-enabled deployments, so synced Zoho credentials can never be refreshed and calendar operations fail once the initial token expires.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the token refresh call is wrapped with `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and the result is stored in `zohoCrmTokenInfo`, but the subsequent logic still assumes an Axios response (`if (!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error)`). In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, it returns the result of `fetch(...)`, i.e. a Fetch `Response` object which has no `.data` property. Therefore, with sharing enabled, `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` is `undefined` and `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` will throw a TypeError.
